outcome: Short-term respiratory morbidities (delayed transitional period, transient desaturation, transient tachypnea of the newborns, requirement of oxygen supplementation)
Short-term non-respiratory morbidities (hypothermia, hypoglycemia, jaundice requiring phototherapy, septic evaluations, admission to a special care nursery, total length of stays, readmission)
cohort: The study included 1,800 neonates (900 early term and 900 full term) born between January 1, 2018, and December 31, 2021, at Ramathibodi Hospital, Mahidol University, Thailand.
finding: Early term neonates had significantly increased risks of both short-term respiratory and non-respiratory morbidities compared to full term neonates.
followup_time: Short-term, encompassing the immediate neonatal period and readmission.
gest_age: Early term at 37 to 38+6 weeks and full term at 39 to 40+6 weeks of gestation.
